docs.title: worldarray
docs.text:
Chunked arrays in world coordinates, through tensorstore.

pip install worldarray

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
Volumetric data lives in zarr v2, zarr v3, N5 and Neuroglancer precomputed stores, on local disks, S3, GCS and HTTP. Each format records where the array sits, its voxel size, origin, units and axes, in its own dialect, and the dialects disagree on the one thing that matters most: whether a stored origin means the centre of the first voxel or its corner. Get that wrong and every object is half a voxel out of place, which is invisible in a viewer and ruinous in a measurement.

Reading such a volume correctly means parsing all those dialects, knowing the half-voxel rule for each, picking a pyramid level for a wanted resolution, and reading a region given in physical units as a plain numpy block, padded where the region leaves the data, resampled when no level matches, fast enough for a model server or a thousand cluster workers, with retries for flaky object stores and thread caps for shared hosts. No one package did all of that, so every tool wrote its own reader, and the readers drifted apart. worldarray is that reader, written once, with the rules stated and tested.

Its dependencies are tensorstore and numpy. Since 0.2 it also writes the one thing every tool wrote for itself and got wrong in its own way: the OME-NGFF metadata of a placed array or pyramid level, and the array itself, created once and filled by aligned writes from any number of jobs. It never deletes, overwrites or downsamples. The specification is the contract it is built to; every rule below is a test.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import worldarray as wa

vol = wa.open("s3://janelia-cosem-datasets/jrc_hela-2/jrc_hela-2.zarr/recon-1/em/fibsem-uint8", level="s1")
vol.voxel_size      # (8.0, 8.0, 8.0) nm, spatial axes
vol.translation     # the centre of voxel 0, in nm
vol.corner          # the lower corner of voxel 0
vol.shape, vol.dtype, vol.axes, vol.levels

box = ((1000.0, 2000.0, 3000.0), (1512.0, 2512.0, 3512.0))   # [begin, end) in nm, half-open
arr = vol.read(box)                            # numpy, z y x; a voxel is read iff its centre lies in the box
arr = vol.read(box, padding="edge")            # a box past the data comes back padded, never raises
arr = vol.read(box, voxel_size=(16, 16, 16))   # resampled on the fly
arr, inside = vol.read(box, mask=True)         # True where the data was

# a volume at a resolution the store does not have: the best level, resampled
six = wa.open(path, voxel_size=(6, 6, 6), on_mismatch="resample")

# one volume read onto another volume's grid, for masks, contact sites, statistics
onto = raw.read(box, voxel_size=labels.voxel_size, anchor=labels.corner)
onto = raw.read_onto(grid, begin, end)   # voxels [begin, end) of a Grid, exactly that shape

# index space, native units: what an engine or a viewer wants
vol = wa.open(path, units=None)
vol.meta            # shape, dtype, chunk_shape, axes, units, voxel_size, translation, attrs, ...
vol.ts              # the tensorstore itself, C order, origin 0
vol.read_index((0, 0, 0), (64, 64, 64), padding=0)

pyr = wa.open_pyramid(path)             # every level, opened on first use
pyr.select((16, 16, 16), mode="floor")  # the level to read at 16 nm

# writing: a placed level, its OME-NGFF group document written for it (zarr v3 + OME 0.5 here)
out = wa.create("out.zarr/s0", shape=(512, 512, 512), dtype="uint64",
                voxel_size=(8, 8, 8), translation=(4, 4, 4), chunks=(64, 64, 64))
out.write_index((0, 0, 0), (64, 64, 64), block)       # whole chunks only: many jobs, no locks
out.write(box, block)                                  # or by world box
s1 = wa.open_pyramid("out.zarr", mode="r+").add_level("s1", factors=2)   # placed and sized; you fill it

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Opens zarr v2, zarr v3 (sharded or not), N5 and precomputed (sharded or not) arrays and pyramids by path, local or s3://, gs://, http(s)://, through tensorstore only. Public buckets are read anonymously first, credentials only when refused; the way in is remembered. AWS_ENDPOINT_URL points at S3-compatible stores.
  • Places every array by one written rule per format (below), reads axes and units as stored, converts only where asked (nanometres by default on spatial axes), and keeps voxel sizes as floats, never rounded.
  • Chooses a level by voxel size from the pyramid's own metadata, without opening the levels, with four policies for a size no level has: error, resample, relabel (voxel i stays voxel i, the grid rescaled), or keep the level.
  • Reads voxel boxes or world boxes as C-contiguous numpy in native byte order, padded with any value or the edge voxel, with an optional mask of what was data, a per-read transform applied before padding (or post_transform after resampling), and resampling by nearest neighbour or linear interpolation anchored where you say. Adjoining block reads agree with one read across both.
  • Behaves on a cluster: one shared tensorstore context per process, its threads sized from WORLDARRAY_THREADS (a job script's share for each worker), OMP_NUM_THREADS or the LSF job's slots instead of the node's cores, or a capped one per worker; reads and writes retried with backoff and size-aware timeouts on transient store errors, a cancelled future on timeout, and every context's thread pools nudged once a second against a tensorstore bug that can leave a queued task with no thread, so a stuck operation recovers or fails loudly instead of hanging the job.
  • Carries the geometry: Box with intersect, union, contains, grow, shift, snap to a grid, and the voxel indices a world box selects.
  • Writes placed arrays (0.2): the OME-NGFF 0.4 or 0.5 document from voxel size, centre translation, axes and units, with each level's placement explicit or derived from factors and an origin; create following the container's format and writing the group documents an output needs down from its .zarr root, with explicit chunks and codecs, and only two answers to "it exists": raise, or adopt an identical array after checking; whole-unit writes from many processes with no coordination; add_level as metadata plus an empty array; chunk keys for every format. Nothing is ever deleted or overwritten.
  • Plans outputs and blocks (0.3): a store-less Grid with the same geometry as an array, so an output is planned, cut into blocks and only then created; blocks tiling an array or a box into write boxes with context-grown read boxes, in C order, as plain picklable records a cluster job takes by id; the anisotropy-aware pyramid schedule; every input read onto that grid by its voxel indices (0.4). Nothing is scheduled or run.

docs.title: The placement rule
docs.text:
A translation is where the centre of voxel 0 is. Index i sits at translation + i * voxel_size and covers half a voxel either side, so the array's corner is corner = translation - voxel_size / 2. With 8 nm voxels and the corner at 0, the translation is 4: voxel 0 covers 0 to 8 nm around its centre at 4, voxel 1 covers 8 to 16 nm around 12. That is how OME-NGFF defines it and how Neuroglancer draws it.

The centre is the model because a voxel is a sample taken at a point. Everything that compares or resamples grids (picking a level, reading one volume onto another's grid, interpolating) works on those points, and the box a voxel covers follows from its point. The read rule follows too: a voxel is read iff its centre lies in the box, so boxes that adjoin never share a voxel or drop one.

Dialects that store the corner are moved half a voxel on reading:

Stored Means Read as translation OME-NGFF translation centre as is COSEM transform.translate centre as is offset beside resolution / voxel_size (offset missing: 0) corner offset + voxel_size / 2 N5 pixelResolution or resolution with downsamplingFactors f, no offset corner at the origin at every level, as Neuroglancer draws N5 f / 2 * base precomputed voxel_offset corner (voxel_offset + 1/2) * resolution nothing a plain array voxels of 1, corner at the origin

Axes are the store's C order; N5 and precomputed are transposed to it. Unlisted or conflicting attributes warn; a voxel size that disagrees with the OME scale raises, since that is how stale metadata is caught. Metadata the parser did not consume stays available raw. The full precedence per format, the half-voxel rules, and every read behaviour are in the specification.

docs.title: API in brief
docs.text:
wa.open(path, *, level=None, voxel_size=None, level_mode="floor", on_mismatch="error",
        padding=0, method="nearest", select=None, units="nanometer", context=None, retries=None,
        metadata_conflicts="error", base_voxel_size=None, base_units=None, anchor=None,
        transform=None, strict_units=True) -> WorldArray
wa.open_pyramid(path, ...) -> Pyramid          # .names .levels .by_name() .select() .placements() .metas(): no opens needed
wa.metadata(path, level=None, units=None, open=True, retries=None) -> ArrayMeta   # open=False: from documents alone
wa.detect(path, missing_ok=False, retries=None) -> Node      # format, array or group, raw attrs
wa.open_tensorstore(path, level=None, context=None, retries=None)
                    # retries= times out and retries document reads and the open, as it does data reads
wa.shared_context(cache_bytes=0, threads=None, fsync=False, locking="none", file_io_floor=8) ; wa.Retry(...)
wa.capped_context(cache_bytes=0, concurrency=1, network=True, file_io=None, fsync=False, locking="none")
wa.thread_budget()                              # the shared context's decoding threads: WORLDARRAY_THREADS, OMP_NUM_THREADS,
                                                #   the job's slots, or CPUs; file I/O gets at least file_io_floor (8);
                                                #   threads=N limits both to N, threads=0 leaves tensorstore's sizes
                                                # contexts made here write without fsync or OS file locks; fsync=True, locking="os" restore them
wa.list_chunk_keys(path, separator=".")        # chunk indices from keys alone, no metadata needed
wa.Box ; wa.units.TABLE

# writing (0.2)
wa.create(path, shape, dtype, voxel_size, translation, *, axes=None, units="nanometer", chunks=..., shards=None,
          fill_value=0, codecs="zstd", format=None, attrs=None, group_attrs=None, exists="error", store_fill=False) -> WorldArray
wa.open(path, mode="r+") ; wa.open_pyramid(path, mode="r+").add_level(name, factors=, origin=0, ...)
wa.ome_multiscales(axes, units, levels, version="0.5", type=None) ; wa.level_placement(voxel_size, translation, factors, origin=0)
wa.level_shape(shape, factors, origin=0) ; wa.chunk_key(index, format, ...) ; wa.parse_chunk_key(key, format, ...)
wa.ensure_group_entry(group_path, name, voxel_size, translation, axes, units="nanometer")   # list an array you made yourself
wa.units.ome_name("nm") -> "nanometer" ; wa.write.codecs_of(path) -> (codecs, shards)

# grids and blocks (0.3)
g = wa.Grid(shape, voxel_size, translation, axes=None, units="nanometer", chunks=None, shards=None)   # or Grid.from_meta(meta, voxel_size=)
wa.create(path, grid=g, dtype="uint64")
for b in wa.blocks(shape, block_shape, context=0, box=None, clip=True):   # also vol.blocks() and g.blocks()
    b.begin, b.end, b.read_begin, b.read_end, b.inner, b.at_end, b.id    # plain records; blocks[id] is O(1)
wa.level_factors(voxel_size, ratio=1.5, max_levels=None, stop_shape=None, shape=None)
wa.units.abbreviation("nanometer") ; wa.store.join(path, "s0") ; wa.store.parent(path) ; wa.store.basename(path)

WorldArray: ts, meta, grid, shape, dtype, axes, voxel_size, translation, corner, box, levels, level_name, level_path, source_voxel_size, source_translation, resampled, writable, write_shape; read(box, voxel_size=, padding=, method=, mask=, anchor=, transform=, post_transform=, select=, strict=), read_index(begin, end, padding=, mask=, select=, transform=), read_onto(grid, begin=, end=, ...), index_box(box), chunks_covering(begin, end, write=), list_chunks(), chunk_key(index), parse_chunk_key(key), write_index(begin, end, data, partial=, retries=) and write(box, data, partial=, retries=) (data an array or a scalar), reopen(context=).

A box is a (begin, end) pair of floats in your units, half-open per axis, over the spatial axes or every axis; any object with .begin/.end or .offset/.shape also works. There is no offset attribute, because that word means the corner in some dialects and the centre in others: translation and corner are the two names for the two things.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: The vocabulary, an array that knows its voxel_size, where it sits and its axis names, and is read by a box in world units, follows funlib.persistence's Array, which many of the tools this serves were built on. The placement rules were consolidated from the readers those tools had each written, in cellmap-flow, cellmap-analyze, mesh-n-bone and chunkmirage, whose conventions document and conformance tests seeded this one; their authors' sessions trialled every change here on their own data. The voxel-centre convention is OME-NGFF's and ITK's, and is what Neuroglancer draws. tensorstore does the work underneath.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
uv sync --group dev --group docs
uv run pytest -q
uv run ruff check src tests && uv run ruff format src tests
uv run mkdocs serve

BSD-3-Clause, Howard Hughes Medical Institute.

A fix for exit. No placement change, no unit table change, and no default changes.

  • The watchdog thread stops at exit, before the interpreter finalizes. On Python up to 3.13 a process could abort once all its work was done ("terminate called without an active exception", exit 134) when finalization began while the thread was inside a tensorstore call; an LSF job that did this looked failed. Now an atexit handler, which runs once the program's other threads are joined, ends the thread and waits for it, and no new one starts after that.

A job script can size each worker's threads. No placement change, no unit table change, and no default changes: with WORLDARRAY_THREADS unset and no file_io_floor, every context is what 0.8 made.

  • thread_budget() reads WORLDARRAY_THREADS ahead of OMP_NUM_THREADS and the job's slots, for a job script to give each dask worker its share of the job's cores where OMP_NUM_THREADS stays 1 for numpy and LSB_DJOB_NUMPROC counts the whole job (for example max(1, ncpus // processes)). A handle opened on the driver on the shared context is sized in each worker by that worker's value. Anything but a positive integer raises ValueError; blank is unset.
  • shared_context(file_io_floor=) sets the least the file I/O pool takes under the thread budget (default FILE_IO_FLOOR, 8); 1 keeps file I/O at the budget. A pickle carries it, and with threads=N or threads=0 it is ignored.

Faster writes from the contexts the package makes, and the create open timed out. No placement change and no unit table change. Requires tensorstore 0.1.68 or later (was 0.1.60), the first with the file_io_locking setting.

  • shared_context and capped_context write without fsync (file_io_sync: false) and without OS file locks (file_io_locking mode "none"); fsync=True and locking="os" restore tensorstore's defaults. A whole-unit write stays atomic, a temporary file renamed into place; only concurrent read-modify-writes of one unit (partial=True) lose their guarantee, which was never given (Behaviour 13). fsync cost 6.5 ms a chunk on a local disk and nothing on NFS; the locks cost about 10 ms a chunk on NFS.
  • The default context's file I/O pool is thread_budget() or 8, whichever is larger; decoding stays at thread_budget(). File I/O threads wait on storage rather than compute, and one of them wrote a block's chunk files one NFS round trip after another. capped_context(file_io=) sizes it apart from concurrency (default unchanged).
  • From one-thread workers through the default context, against 0.7: a 64^3 label chunk to NFS 23 to 12.2 ms (zarr-python 2: 13.1), an 8-chunk label block 159 to 66.5 ms (zarr-python 2: 102), an 8-chunk EM block 330 to 202 ms; to a local disk a label block 51.5 to 4.1 ms. Through capped_context(1, network=False) the NFS label block went 166 to 91 ms; file_io=8 gives it the rest.
  • The open that creates an array is timed out and retried under retries (Behaviour 6). A retry that finds the array made by an attempt of its own that timed out adopts it after the usual comparison, even under exists="error". That open keeps OS locking, so create-if-absent stays atomic.

Faster opens over http. No placement change, no unit table change, no API change.

  • The documents a call needs from one directory are read at once instead of in turn. An http open of a zarr v2 level made its eight requests one after another (five probe keys, the level's .zattrs, the parent's zarr.json and .zattrs); now they go in three rounds. At 10 ms an answer, wa.open took 98 ms and takes 52 (cellmap-flow's measurement). A server that never answers still costs one key's attempts, not five.

Opens time out. No placement change and no unit table change.

  • Every metadata document read or written and every store opened is timed out and retried under Retry, as data reads are (Behaviour 6): by default 5 s times the attempt, ten attempts. A server that accepts a connection and never answers held wa.open and wa.metadata forever before; it now raises TimeoutError naming the URL and the attempts (cellmap-flow, 2026-10-23). The policy is the call's retries, which wa.metadata, wa.detect and wa.open_tensorstore now take as wa.open, wa.open_pyramid and wa.create already did. Listings and the open that creates an array are not timed out.

One new argument, at chunkmirage's request. No placement change and no unit table change; nothing changes for a caller that does not pass it.

  • wa.shared_context(cache_bytes, threads=): None (the default) limits the decoding and file I/O pools to thread_budget() as in 0.5, a positive number limits them to that many, and 0 writes no limit, so tensorstore sizes them itself (every CPU on the node). Each (cache_bytes, threads) is one watched context for the process, so a server can share one cache pool across every store it opens at the thread count it chose, without building and watching its own context. A pickled handle on such a context comes back on the same one; threads=None still lets the other process size by its own job.
  • Documented what a pool of one thread costs (spec Behaviour 7, capped_context_spec): nothing on one-chunk blocks; on 8-chunk blocks, half the speed of 4 in a two-slot job but only 7 to 19% slower in a one-slot one (c-elegans on /nrs), so a worker per slot loses little at the default.

Two bugs that hung or crashed cellmap-analyze 0.6 on /nrs (salamander's and c-elegans' runs, 2026-10-22), and tensorstore's threads sized to the job. No placement change and no unit table change.

  • A read whose first attempt timed out raised IndexError instead of retrying: the warning took the first line of the error's message, and tensorstore's TimeoutError() has none. The warning now names the error's type when the message is empty, and the error after the last attempt names the operation, the path and the attempts.
  • Every context the package makes or opens a store on is watched: once a second a daemon thread gives its decoding and file I/O pools one no-op task each (an in-memory copy and a local read of a missing key; no store is touched). tensorstore up to at least 0.1.85 can strand a queued task: a pool worker idle for 20 ms exits as the task arrives, and the task never runs (fixed upstream in google/tensorstore ed51718085, in no release yet). With data_copy and file_io capped at 1, as cellmap-analyze's workers were, dozens of workers per run waited forever in write_index with no tensorstore thread alive, and reads timed out into the IndexError above. One more task on the same pool wakes it, which salamander's and c-elegans' sessions proved on live stuck workers, so a stranded task now runs within about a second, at any concurrency, whoever waits on it: worldarray, vol.ts directly or await. Reproduced on purpose on tensorstore 0.1.75, 0.1.78 and 0.1.85 (opt-in tests/test_lost_wakeup.py): cellmap-analyze's block loop gave 29 IndexErrors and 55 writes stuck past 20 s on 0.4.0, none on 0.5.0, slowest 0.98 s. Spec open question 14 says when this goes.
  • write_index, write and write_chunk are timed out and retried as reads are (Behaviour 6), by a new retries= argument or the handle's retries. A write used to wait on its future with no timeout at all.
  • Without context, the shared context's decoding and file I/O pools are limited to the new wa.thread_budget(): OMP_NUM_THREADS when set (dask sets 1 in each worker), else the job's slots (LSB_DJOB_NUMPROC, SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK, NSLOTS), else the CPUs the process may run on. A server that wants more threads than its job's slots asks for more slots or passes its own context. tensorstore alone sizes both to every CPU on the node, whatever bsub -n asked for, so a dask worker's tensorstore now takes the same one thread as its numpy (pinned to one CPU, tensorstore's default context started 43 to 45 pool threads, the capped one 4 to 5). Against cellmap-analyze 0.5.0's own block I/O on NFS (128^3 uint64 label blocks, each one chunk), its 0.6.1 on this release reads a block in 26 ms instead of 40 and writes it in 45 ms instead of 62 from one process at one thread per pool, and about 1.15 times faster from 8. Speed gains grow with blocks of several chunks and more threads.

cellmap-analyze's three asks, so it can call worldarray directly with no wrapper, and two of cellmap-flow's. No placement change and no unit table change.

  • vol.read_onto(grid, begin=None, end=None, ...) reads voxels [begin, end) of a Grid's spatial axes from the array, exactly that shape (Behaviour 20). It is the read of the grid's index box at the grid's voxel size anchored at its corner, so at the array's own voxel size nothing is resampled, whatever the sub-voxel offset, and otherwise the array is resampled onto the grid. The grid's units are converted.
  • A pickled handle, and reopen, use the path resolved against the working directory at open, so a worker that changes directory before unpickling opens the same store; it used to raise FileNotFoundError for a relative path.
  • write_index, write and write_chunk take a scalar, which fills the box. It is converted to the dtype only when its value survives (0 into uint8; 300, -1, 0.5 and NaN raise), and the fill value over whole units leaves them absent.
  • vol.source_translation: the stored level's translation in units, beside source_voxel_size, under resample and relabel too (cellmap-flow's stored_placement).
  • create(exists="adopt") also compares the keys of attrs with the existing array's attributes and raises naming each that differs or is missing; keys not given are not compared. An adopt given different attrs used to keep the old ones silently, as funlib's prepare_ds kept an old offset (cellmap-flow's _refuse_another_region).

• source_voxel_size reports the stored level's voxel size under on_mismatch="relabel", as the spec says; it reported the relabelled size (cellmap-flow's report). Reads, voxel_size, translation and corner are unchanged.
  • box of an array opened with a resample target is the extent of the target voxels shape counts, as the spec's [corner, corner + shape * voxel_size) says and as Grid.from_meta(meta, voxel_size=t).box already was; it was the stored data's extent, so read(box) could return fewer voxels than shape (cellmap-flow's 7 voxels of 8 nm at 24 nm: box ended at 56 nm, now 72). No voxel moves.
  • Unit table change. The unit table knows kilometres (kilometer, kilometre, km, 1e3 m), so they convert, abbreviate to km and are written as OME's kilometer (chunkmirage's ask). This should have been a minor release (spec section 8): cellmap-flow exports the table and its CI failed until it moved its pin to >=0.3.1.
  • README: the placement rule gains the corner formula, a worked example, why the centre is the model, and how the read rule follows from it.

Grids and blocks, built to spec draft 3 (Behaviours 17 to 19). Nothing on the read or write side changes.

  • blocks(shape, block_shape, context=0, box=None, clip=True): the array (or a voxel box, which may reach past the array) cut into write boxes that tile it with no overlap and no gap, each with a read box grown by context (one int, one per axis, or (before, after) pairs) and clipped to the array when clip; C order, len, blocks[id] in O(1), index_of(begin); a Block carries index, id, begin, end, read_begin, read_end, at_start and at_end per axis and inner, the write box's slices inside the read box. Plain picklable records; nothing is scheduled. vol.blocks() defaults the block to write_shape, so default blocks are aligned writes. vol.write_chunk(index, data) writes one whole unit.
  • Grid(shape, voxel_size, translation, axes, units, chunks, shards): a WorldArray without a store, with box, corner, index_box, chunks_covering, write_shape, blocks and meta(dtype); Grid.from_meta(meta, voxel_size=) is an existing array's grid or the resample target grid over it. create(path, grid=g, dtype=) creates from it.
  • level_factors(voxel_size, ratio=1.5, ...): the anisotropy-aware pyramid schedule mesh-n-bone and cellmap-analyze share, per level.
  • units.abbreviation, and store.join, store.parent, store.basename as public URL-aware path helpers.

Metadata and placed creation, built to spec draft 3 (Behaviours 10 to 16). Nothing on the read side changes.

  • ome_multiscales(axes, units, levels, version) builds the complete OME-NGFF 0.4 or 0.5 group document with one explicit placement per level; level_placement and level_shape derive a level from factors and an origin (Convention 1's rule inverted, so a level built from a ROI origin is placed from it; level_shape absorbs float-noise factors such as 0.3 / 0.1). Units are written in OME's names ("nm" becomes "nanometer"; units.ome_name), an unknown unit as given; the multiscale's type is written when given. Expected documents are pinned in tests/fixtures/write.json, shared with chunkmirage's TypeScript builder, each case with its resolved per-axis units and types, fifteen cases.
  • create(path, shape, dtype, voxel_size, translation, chunks=..., ...) writes the group document (made when absent, else its one dataset entry added or replaced, every other attribute kept) and then the array, as zarr v2 with OME 0.4 or zarr v3 with OME 0.5 following the group's format. chunks is required, codecs are explicit with a zstd level 3 default, shards are a zarr v3 option. exists is "error" or "adopt" (an identical array is opened for writing, a different one raises naming every difference, a creation lost to another process is adopted after a short backoff). Nothing is ever deleted, truncated or overwritten. Write units equal to the fill value are not stored unless store_fill=True, and a stored unit written so loses its key, as zarr-python's write_empty_chunks=False does. create also writes a bare group document for every missing ancestor down from the .zarr root and follows the nearest existing ancestor's zarr version, so a level made in a zarr v2 container is zarr v2 with OME 0.4 and the hierarchy browses (cellmap-analyze, cellmap-flow). Adopting an identical array writes no group document; after a write the document is read again and a lost entry is written again, then raises (registration-station's concurrent block jobs).
  • ensure_group_entry is public: list an array the package did not create, such as a symlinked s0 (mesh-n-bone), or a level filled before it is listed.
  • open(path, mode="r+") opens an existing array for writing; a WorldArray pickles by its arguments and its context's spec and reopens in the receiving process, a capped context staying capped (mesh-n-bone's workers). write.codecs_of takes a path.
  • write_index(begin, end, data) writes whole write units only (the shard when sharded, else the chunk; the clipped last unit allowed), so writers in different processes need no coordination; partial=True does tensorstore's read-modify-write. write(box, data) maps a world box by the centre rule first. No cast, no padding, no resampling on write.
  • open_pyramid(path, mode="r+").add_level(name, factors=, origin=) creates a level's entry and empty array, placed and sized from the level below with its dtype, chunks, shards, codecs and fill value copied; the downsampling itself stays with the caller.
  • chunk_key and parse_chunk_key for zarr v2, zarr v3 (both encodings, sharded arrays keyed by shard), N5 and precomputed, as free functions and on WorldArray; list_chunks uses the same parser. write_shape, ArrayMeta.shard_shape, chunks_covering(write=True).

• funlib voxel_size/offset on the parent group place an array that carries none, for zarr and N5 alike; funlib's keys on an N5 array are read in the array's C order, as zarr-python's N5 store writes them (both from mesh-n-bone's review of its PR #48).
  • A precomputed path that names a scale is that scale under level=0 or "first" too; other levels warn and are ignored, as on an array path.
  • The GCE metadata guard is applied only off Google Cloud (decided from the DMI product name and the GCE_METADATA_* variables), so metadata-server credentials keep working on a Google VM.
  • Pyramid.placements(), voxel_sizes() and translations() read the group document when the pyramid was opened through one of its level paths too; they used to open every level from there, and a missing level made them raise.
  • Placement change. An N5 level with downsamplingFactors and no offset now sits with its corner at the origin at every level, as Neuroglancer draws N5: translation f / 2 * base. 0.1.0 followed BigDataViewer for pixelResolution pyramids, centring the base's voxel 0 on the origin ((f - 1) / 2 * base, half a base voxel lower), while placing resolution pyramids with the corner at the origin, so the two disagreed. Two shared fixture cases move and are renamed: n5_group_pixelresolution_and_downsampling_factors_corner_at_origin (translation 4, 4, 4) and n5_bigstitcher_resolution_with_downsampling_factors_corner_at_origin (0.5, 0.157, 0.157).

• First version, built to docs/spec.md: open zarr v2, zarr v3, N5 and Neuroglancer precomputed arrays and pyramids through tensorstore; one metadata precedence per format with the voxel-centre rule for translations; index-space and world-box reads with padding; level selection; nearest and linear resampling; retries; shared and capped tensorstore contexts. Built and trialled in one day against the readers it replaces in cellmap-flow, cellmap-analyze, mesh-n-bone and chunkmirage, and checked on their own data by the CineMap, liconn-err, registration-station and salamander repos; see docs/spec.md, "Trial status". Hot-path reads cost 0.1 to 0.2 ms over a raw tensorstore read.

docs.title: Specification
docs.text:
worldarray is built to this document. Sections 1 to 5 are also the README; every statement under "Behaviour" and "Tests" is something a test pins. Code that is not needed to make a statement here true does not go in; a behaviour not stated here is not implemented without adding the statement first.

Draft 3, 2026-10-22. Written from a reading of every existing reader in David Ackerman's repos and the answers of the chunkmirage, cellmap-flow, cellmap-analyze, mesh-n-bone, CineMap, liconn-err, registration-station, salamander and cellmap-analyze-scripts sessions; the write side (0.2) and the grid side (0.3) were added on 2026-10-22 from the five writer sessions' answers and the line census in section 6. Decisions still open are in section 7. Version map: 0.1 reads (Behaviours 1 to 9); 0.2 metadata and placed creation (10 to 16); 0.3 grids and blocks (17 to 19). Nothing in 0.2 or 0.3 changes a 0.1 behaviour.

docs.title: 0. Why this exists
docs.text:
Seven readers across those repos open the same zarr v2, zarr v3, N5 and precomputed volumes through tensorstore and each parses the OME-NGFF, COSEM N5 and precomputed metadata by hand: cellmap-flow (image_data_interface.py plus io/, 2.7k lines), cellmap-analyze (765), mesh-n-bone (346), chunkmirage (tensorstore_source.py, 649), CineMap (slice_loader.py), liconn-err (dataset.py) and registration-station (zarr-python, by hand); salamander's analysis scripts parse OME multiscales by hand three more times. They disagree on the one rule that matters, the half voxel between a stored corner and a stored centre: all of them place an OME translation at voxel 0's centre, but mesh-n-bone also reads funlib's offset and precomputed's voxel_offset as centres (both store the corner) and ignores COSEM translate and downsamplingFactors, CineMap's extent_nm() and c-elegans' camera code treat the translation as a corner while their reads treat it as the centre, cellmap-flow learned the OME rule in PR #103 after shipping without it (salamander's predictions were half a voxel off until then), and chunkmirage's TypeScript twin handles N5 differently from its Python.

funlib.persistence has the right vocabulary but the wrong backend for these consumers. What its Array lacks, per cellmap-flow's session: tensorstore (s3, gs and http throughput, the precomputed and zarr v3 drivers; Array reads through zarr-python and dask, and a dask scheduler has no place in a per-chunk model server); reads that run past the array and come back padded (Array.__getitem__ raises on a Roi outside the data; model halos at a volume's edge need the padding); level selection by target voxel size with an explicit mismatch policy; the OME centre rule (funlib's Roi offset is a corner); per-read retries and one shared, capped tensorstore context. Add the zarr-python major-version split across the repos (cellmap-flow pins 2.18.4; cellmap-analyze and mesh-n-bone pin >= 3.0.8; cellmap-analyze dropped funlib.persistence in 2026-04 because it lacked zarr v3), the integer-only Coordinate, and pymongo, psycopg2 and dask as dependencies of a reader. Nothing outside Janelia fills the niche: webknossos-libs, neu-vol, cloud-volume, brainhops, yaozarrs and xarray-tensorstore were all checked on 2026-10-21 and each is a pipeline or a different model, not this dependency.

So: one small package, one class that serves both kinds of consumer, one written rule for the half voxel, and conformance tests the TypeScript side can run too.

The write side has the same disease in a smaller body. Measured on 2026-10-22: five repos generate OME multiscales documents by hand (cellmap-analyze, mesh-n-bone, cellmap-flow, registration-station, chunkmirage; 440 lines between them), five create placed arrays with five different answers to "it already exists" (an unverified adopt zeroed 180 rows of a registration-station field), four encode chunk keys, and every write-side bug their sessions could name was a metadata bug: a scale factor that ignored the corner (cellmap-analyze #93), a level translation that ignored the ROI origin (mesh-n-bone, on master), OME 0.4 attributes inside zarr v3 groups (two repos), a hard-coded nanometre, a funlib offset holding a centre. The bytes were never the problem: they go through tensorstore or zarr-python and nobody reported a byte-level bug. So 0.2 takes the metadata and the placed creation, and nothing else of writing.

docs.title: 1. Scope
docs.text:
One class, WorldArray, with two faces. No legacy names: ImageDataInterface, open_ds_tensorstore and to_ndarray_ts are not in this package; each migrating repo keeps whatever shim it needs in its own subclass, for as long as it needs it.

  • Index space, native units (units=None): .ts, .meta and read_index. For chunkmirage, CineMap, liconn-err, registration-station and any tool that works in its own coordinate frame. The metadata is read exactly as chunkmirage's docs/concepts/formats.md "Stored sources" specifies.
  • World coordinates (units="nanometer" by default, or any unit per axis kind): voxel_size, translation, corner, level selection by voxel size, read of world boxes with padding, optional resampling and retries. For cellmap-flow, cellmap-analyze and mesh-n-bone, which all speak nm and Rois today, and equally for a (t, c, z, y, x) light-microscopy series or a (time, lat, lon) climate array.

Neither face assumes microscopy or three dimensions. Any number of axes, any axis names, any units: what the store says is what the package reports, converted only on the axes it is asked to convert.

0.1 reads. 0.2 adds the write side's metadata and placed creation (Behaviours 10 to 16): the OME document builder and the level rule, chunk keys, create, opening for write, aligned writes, add_level. 0.3 adds grids (Behaviours 17 to 19): a store-less Grid, the block iterator every blockwise repo writes for itself, write_chunk, the factor schedule and the public path helpers. Dependencies at every version: tensorstore (>=0.1.60; >=0.1.68 from 0.8, the first with file_io_locking), numpy. No zarr, no dask, no pydantic, no funlib. The package is float-only; a consumer that works in integer Rois builds them in its own subclass (section 6). Python >= 3.10 with no 3.11-only syntax, no upper bounds on numpy or tensorstore.

The package never deletes, truncates or overwrites: there is no overwrite, delete or mode="w" anywhere in its API (Behaviour 11). What it writes is OME-NGFF zarr, v2 with OME 0.4 or v3 with OME 0.5, and nothing else (Convention 6).

Not in scope, by decision, each with its consumer named so it is not forgotten:

Out of scope Who asked Where it lives instead Deleting or overwriting arrays and groups, following symlinks, "rmtree before rerun" every writer repo, by consensus on 2026-10-22 each repo's own policy: cellmap-analyze's delete_tmp_dir_blockwise, mesh-n-bone's _safely_remove_pyramid, cellmap-flow's never-delete rules Downsampling and its reducers (mode, mean, median, min, max, majority vote), the pyramid compute cellmap-analyze #90, mesh-n-bone, registration-station, cellmap-flow each repo, per block, through write_index; add_level writes a level's metadata and empty array only Block scheduling: dask, daisy, LSF, OOM retry, memory sizing every blockwise repo each repo; 0.3's iterator yields boxes and runs nothing Writing N5 or precomputed; serving-policy documents (.zarray codecs, info); writing exactly the bytes served chunkmirage chunkmirage's frontends and materialize, which call the builder and chunk_key for the placement half Arbitrary affines, BigStitcher XML, OME 0.6 coordinate systems and RFC-5 transforms liconn-err, chunkmirage liconn-err; chunkmirage's ngff.py and scene://. The reader takes an OME 0.6 group's intrinsic system (Convention 4) and no more Oblique-plane sampling, chunk-grouped gather CineMap CineMap, on top of .ts and chunks_covering CF packing (scale_factor, add_offset, _FillValue), xarray coordinate arrays chunkmirage chunkmirage, from ArrayMeta.attrs, group_attrs and parent, which the package exposes raw HDF5, GeoTIFF chunkmirage chunkmirage Normalisation chains, model-facing defaults cellmap-flow a cellmap_flow subclass of WorldArray The integer-scaled frame cellmap-analyze dropped, not moved: its commands work in voxel indices of their own output grid and read inputs with read(box, voxel_size=, anchor=) (its session's decision, 2026-10-22); mesh-n-bone and cellmap-flow keep their own funlib bridges Legacy write documents (funlib voxel_size/offset, COSEM transform) as package output cellmap-analyze, whose outputs dacapo may read through funlib the attrs passthrough of create; Open question 5 Decoded-chunk caches beyond tensorstore's pool, demand queues, serving chunkmirage chunkmirage

docs.title: 2. Public API
docs.text:
import worldarray as wa

vol = wa.open(
    path,                # an array, a level under a multiscale group, or a group
    level=None,          # a level name ("s1"), a position (0 = the first listed, "first"), or None;
                         #   ignored, with a warning, for an array path
    voxel_size=None,     # the size to read at, in `units`: picks the level (level_mode); see on_mismatch
    level_mode="floor",  # "floor" | "finer" | "exact" | "nearest" | "resample" (Behaviour 3)
    on_mismatch="error", # when no level has `voxel_size`: "error" (list the levels) | "resample" (read the
                         #   level `level_mode` picks and resample it, Behaviour 4) | "relabel" (read it voxel
                         #   for voxel and call its voxels `voxel_size`; no resampling, the grid is relabelled;
                         #   cellmap-flow's default, which its finetune reads rely on) | "keep" (the level
                         #   `level_mode` picks, at its own voxel size: cellmap-analyze's target_voxel_size)
    padding=0,           # any value the dtype holds (0, NaN, a uint64 sentinel) | "edge": what fills the
                         #   part of a box outside the data
    method="nearest",    # "nearest" | "linear": the resampling kernel; no dtype heuristic (Behaviour 5)
    select=None,         # {"c": 0, "t": 0}: pin non-spatial axes to one index; else they are kept whole
    units="nanometer",   # what world coordinates are in on spatial axes; a dict per axis kind
                         #   ({"space": "micrometer", "time": "second"}); None keeps the store's own units
    context=None,        # a tensorstore.Context; default shared_context(0)
    retries=None,        # a Retry; default Retry()
    metadata_conflicts="error",  # a per-array voxel_size disagreeing with the OME scale: "error" | "warn"
    base_voxel_size=None,  # declare level 0's true voxel size (in base_units): every level's spatial voxel
    base_units=None,       #   size and translation scale with it, for stores whose metadata is in voxels or unitless
    anchor=None,           # where a target voxel corner lies when resampling; the source corner by default
    transform=None,        # a callable applied to stored values before resampling and padding (a norm chain)
                         #   read(..., post_transform=) runs one after resampling instead, still before padding
    strict_units=True,     # False: an unknown unit ("pixel") is taken as the target unit, with a warning
)

vol.ts             # tensorstore.TensorStore: C-order axes, origin 0, selected axes dropped
vol.meta           # ArrayMeta in the store's own units
vol.grid           # ArrayMeta in the requested units, every axis
vol.shape, vol.dtype, vol.axes, vol.spatial, vol.level_name, vol.levels, vol.remote
                   # shape is the stored shape, or with a resample target the target voxels covering the data
vol.source_voxel_size, vol.source_translation, vol.resampled
                   # the stored level's voxel size and translation (0.4), also under resample and relabel; whether
                   #   reads resample to a target
vol.list_chunks()  # the chunk indices that exist in storage, by listing keys (zarr v2/v3, N5, unsharded precomputed)
vol.path           # what the caller passed (a group, say); vol.level_path is the array actually opened
vol.voxel_size     # tuple[float] in `units`, spatial axes, the array's order (zyx for a volume)
vol.translation    # tuple[float] in `units`: the CENTRE of voxel 0        (OME-NGFF's word, OME-NGFF's meaning)
vol.corner         # tuple[float] in `units`: translation - voxel_size / 2 (what funlib, daisy, Neuroglancer call the offset)
vol.retries        # settable after construction (cellmap-analyze scales the timeout per handle)
vol.padding, vol.method   # the defaults `read` uses; settable

vol.read_index(begin, end, padding=None, mask=False, retries=None, select=None, transform=None)
                                    # select pins axes for this read only; begin/end cover the rest
vol.read(box, voxel_size=None, padding=None, method=None, mask=False, retries=None, strict=False, anchor=None,
         transform=None, post_transform=None, select=None)   # select pins non-spatial axes for this read
vol.index_box(box) -> (begin, end)  # the voxels a world box selects on this grid, for snapping a box first
vol.chunks_covering(begin, end)     # chunk indices a voxel box touches
vol.reopen(context=None, **overrides) -> WorldArray   # the same array on another context (a worker changing its concurrency)

pyr = wa.open_pyramid(path, context=None, units="nanometer", select=None)
pyr.names; pyr.levels; pyr.by_name("s1"); pyr.select(voxel_size, mode="floor")
pyr.metas() ; pyr.level_meta("s1")   # ArrayMeta per level from the documents alone: shape, dtype, chunks (a sharded
                    #   array's inner chunk), fill and placement, with no tensorstore opened
pyr.placements()    # (name, spatial voxel size, spatial translation) per level from the group's own document
pyr.voxel_sizes() ; pyr.translations()   #   where it lists the levels (OME-NGFF, COSEM N5, precomputed), so
                    #   choosing or placing a level opens nothing, whether the pyramid was opened by its
                    #   group path or by one of its level paths; else by opening each level

wa.metadata(path, level=None, units=None, open=True, retries=None) -> ArrayMeta   # open=False: from the documents alone
wa.detect(path, missing_ok=False, retries=None) -> Node | None   # format, kind (array|group), path, docs, scale_key; .attrs (raw user
                                                   #   attributes), .multiscales (OME 0.5's `ome` unwrapped)
wa.open_tensorstore(path, level=None, context=None, retries=None) -> tensorstore.TensorStore   # reads no world metadata, so an
                                                   #   array with odd placement attributes (a coordinate array) still opens
wa.corner_to_centre(corner, voxel_size, axes=None) ; wa.default_axes(ndim) ; wa.index_range(begin, end, voxel_size, translation)
wa.units.TABLE      # the unit tables, public: {"length": {...metres per unit}, "time": {...seconds per unit}}
wa.select_level(levels, voxel_size, mode) ; wa.Box ; wa.Retry(max_attempts=10, timeout=None, base_delay=1.0)
wa.shared_context(cache_bytes=0, threads=None, fsync=False, locking="none", file_io_floor=8)
wa.capped_context(cache_bytes=0, concurrency=1, network=True, file_io=None, fsync=False, locking="none") ; wa.capped_context_spec(...)
                    # threads: None = thread_budget() for decoding and at least file_io_floor for file I/O (0.8; the
                    #   argument 0.9), N = that many, 0 = tensorstore's own pool sizes (0.6); fsync and locking:
                    #   tensorstore's file_io_sync and file_io_locking mode, off and "none" in every context the
                    #   package makes (0.8, Behaviour 7)
                    # network=False caps decoding and local file I/O only, leaving tensorstore's request pools alone
wa.list_chunk_keys(path, separator=".", ndim=None)   # chunk indices present under a path, from its keys alone: no
                    #   metadata document needed, so a directory of chunk files with no .zarray lists too

ArrayMeta is a frozen dataclass with one entry per axis, in the array's C order, and deliberately the same field names as chunkmirage's ArrayInfo: shape, dtype, chunk_shape (tensorstore's read chunk), axes (as stored; ("t","c","z","y","x")[-ndim:] when the store names none), axes_named, units (as stored, any string; "" when none), voxel_size (one index step, in units; 1.0 on unitless axes), translation (the centre of voxel 0, in units; 0.0 where the store gives none), format, path (normalised), parent, attrs and group_attrs (raw), and placed_by: which rule gave voxel_size and translation, one of ome, cosem, funlib, n5, precomputed, dimension_units, or None when nothing placed the array (then voxel size is 1 with the corner at the origin, translation 0.5, as Neuroglancer draws a plain zarr), and fill_value as the store reports it. Derived: ndim, spatial (indices of the axes named z, y or x when any are; else the last three), corner, in_units(space=, time=), in_nm(), drop_axis.

A box for read is any of: a (begin, end) pair of float tuples in units, half-open per axis, over the spatial axes, or over every axis when it has one entry per axis (a time window and a spatial box at once); anything with .begin and .end, or .offset and .shape (so a funlib Roi works, duck-typed, without the package importing funlib); or wa.Box. Box carries funlib's Roi vocabulary on floats, half-open: shape, centre, empty, intersect, union, contains (a point or a box), grow(before, after=None), shift, snap(voxel_size, translation, mode="grow" | "shrink" | "closest") to a grid's voxel corners, to_index (the centre rule) and Box.from_index; vol.box is the array's own extent on the spatial axes, [corner, corner + shape * voxel_size), what funlib calls the array's roi; with a resample target, the target voxels shape counts, so read(vol.box) returns shape and equals Grid.from_meta(meta, voxel_size=t).box. So vol.read(vol.box.intersect(roi).snap(vol.voxel_size, vol.translation)) is the migration of a clipped, snapped Roi read, without funlib.

There is no offset attribute anywhere in this API, because that word means the corner in funlib and the centre in OME; translation and corner are the two names for the two things. path names the array that is read: an array path is that array whatever voxel_size asks for (it resamples or relabels in place, never hops to a sibling level); only a group path chooses a level. level="first" or 0 on an array path is silently the array. There is no funlib Roi on the way out either: an integer corner-based Roi cannot hold a 10.48 nm grid, nor a 5 nm grid with translation 0 (corner -2.5), so a bridge that returned one would raise on inputs cellmap-analyze reads every day. A consumer that works in integer Rois builds them from corner, voxel_size and shape in its own subclass, where it also chooses the integer scale factor that makes the corner whole.

shared_context(cache_bytes, threads=None) is one tensorstore.Context per budget and thread limit for the process, so the levels of a pyramid and repeat opens share one cache pool; the default budget is 0. Its decoding pool is sized by thread_budget() (0.5) and its file I/O pool by that or file_io_floor (8), whichever is larger (0.8; the argument 0.9), or both by threads when given, 0 leaving tensorstore's own sizes (0.6, Behaviour 7). capped_context is mesh-n-bone's worker-process context (every tensorstore concurrency resource limited, cache off); it returns a new context per call, as those workers inline the spec into every open today, and capped_context_spec exports the dict for callers building their own opens, writers included. Retry sizes the per-attempt timeout from the read when none is given (Behaviour 6).

docs.title: 0.2: metadata and placed creation
docs.text:
Module worldarray.write, re-exported at the top level. Nothing here is imported by the read side, so a read-only consumer sees no change.

doc = wa.ome_multiscales(
    axes,                 # axis names in the array's C order: ("z","y","x"), ("c","z","y","x"), ("t","c","z","y","x")
        units,                # per axis ("nanometer"; "" on a channel axis) or by kind {"space": "nanometer", "time": "second"};
                          #   written in OME's names ("nm" -> "nanometer", wa.units.ome_name), an unknown unit as given
    levels,               # [("s0", voxel_size, translation), ...]: one explicit placement per level over the spatial axes
                          #   (or every axis). Never derived here: levels in the wild carry their own translations and
                          #   non-whole factors (chunkmirage's pyramids)
    version="0.5",        # "0.5" (zarr v3: attributes["ome"]) | "0.4" (zarr v2: attributes["multiscales"])
    axis_types=None,      # per axis "space" | "time" | "channel"; default from the name (z y x space, t time, c channel)
        name="", metadata=None, type=None,   # the multiscale's own fields; `type` (the downsampling method) written when given
) -> dict                 # the complete group attributes to write; `wa.metadata` reads them back exactly (Behaviour 10)

wa.level_placement(voxel_size, translation, factors, origin=0) -> (voxel_size, translation)
                          # the level whose voxel j covers source voxels origin + j f .. origin + (j + 1) f - 1 on each axis:
                          #   (voxel_size * f, translation + voxel_size * (origin + (f - 1) / 2)). Convention 1's BigDataViewer
                          #   rule inverted, and the centre Behaviour 4's block mean produces
wa.level_shape(shape, factors, origin=0) -> shape    # ceil((n - origin) / f) per axis, the quotient snapped to a whole
                                                     #   number within 1e-6 first (0.3 / 0.1 is a factor of 3)
wa.units.ome_name(unit) -> str   # OME's name for any spelling the unit table knows ("nanometer" for "nm"); unknown raises
wa.ensure_group_entry(group_path, name, voxel_size, translation, axes, units="nanometer", axis_types=None,
                      group_attrs=None, format=None)   # list an array the package did not create (a symlinked s0, a level
                          #   filled before it is listed): the group document's entry for `name` added or replaced, the
                          #   document and missing ancestors created, nothing written when the entry already says the same
                          #   (Behaviour 12). `create` and `add_level` call this
wa.write.codecs_of(path_or_node) -> (codecs, shards)   # an array's codecs in its format's dialect and its shard shape, for
                          #   a mirror created like it (cellmap-flow's sync)

vol = wa.create(
    path,                 # ".../vol.zarr/s0": the last component is the level, its parent the multiscale group, made if absent
    shape, dtype,
    voxel_size, translation,   # spatial placement in `units`, or one entry per axis
    axes=None, units="nanometer",   # as ome_multiscales; axes default to default_axes(ndim)
    chunks=...,           # required: the storage chunk (the inner chunk when sharded). The package never picks a chunk shape
    shards=None,          # zarr v3 only: the shard shape, a whole number of chunks per axis
    fill_value=0,
    codecs="zstd",        # "zstd" (level 3, which is what zarr-python's default `zstd(level=0)` means) | "none" | the format's
                          #   own JSON: a zarr v2 `compressor` dict or a zarr v3 `codecs` list
        format=None,          # "zarr3" | "zarr2"; default the nearest existing ancestor group's format, else "zarr3"; missing
                          #   ancestors up to the ".zarr" root get bare group documents (Behaviour 11).
                          #   OME 0.5 goes with v3 and 0.4 with v2, always
    attrs=None,           # extra array attributes, merged into the array's own
    group_attrs=None,     # extra group attributes, merged; no one else's key is dropped or rewritten (Behaviour 12)
    exists="error",       # "error": anything already at `path` raises | "adopt": an identical array (shape, dtype, chunks,
                          #   shards, placement within rtol 1e-6, and from 0.4 every key of `attrs` holding the value given)
                          #   is opened for writing; a different one raises naming each
                                                    #   difference. There is no third value. An adopt writes no group document when the entry
                          #   already says the same (Behaviour 12)
    store_fill=False,     # True stores write units equal to fill_value instead of leaving them absent
    separator=None,       # zarr v2 dimension_separator, zarr v3 chunk-key separator; the format's default when None
    axis_types=None,      # as ome_multiscales
    context=None, retries=None,
) -> WorldArray           # writable; every read-side property and method as before

vol = wa.open(path, mode="r+", store_fill=False, ...)   # an existing array for writing; vol.writable; the metadata
                                                                                                                #   rules of mode "r" unchanged; a handle pickles by its arguments
                                                        #   and its context's spec (Behaviour 11)
vol.write_index(begin, end, data, partial=False)   # whole write units only (Behaviour 13) unless partial
vol.write(box, data, partial=False)                # a world box by Behaviour 2, then write_index; no padding, no resampling
vol.write_shape                                    # the unit one writer may own: the shard shape when sharded, else the chunk shape
vol.chunks_covering(begin, end, write=False)       # write=True: on the write-unit grid
vol.chunk_key(index) -> str ; vol.parse_chunk_key(key) -> tuple[int, ...] | None   # storage keys of write units (Behaviour 15)
wa.chunk_key(index, format, separator="/", encoding="default", chunk_shape=None, shape=None, origin=None) -> str
wa.parse_chunk_key(key, format, ...) -> tuple[int, ...] | None    # the same from the array's facts alone, for an array that is
                                                   #   served from nowhere (chunkmirage) or not yet created

pyr = wa.open_pyramid(path, mode="r+")
pyr.add_level(name, factors=None, origin=0, voxel_size=None, translation=None, shape=None, dtype=None, chunks=None,
              shards=None, codecs=None, fill_value=None, attrs=None, exists="error", from_level=None) -> WorldArray
                          # the level's dataset entry and its empty array: placement by level_placement over `from_level`
                          #   (the finest listed when None) unless given explicitly, shape by level_shape, dtype, chunks,
                          #   shards, codecs and fill copied from that level unless given; no voxel data; one process at a time

docs.text:
Module worldarray.grid, re-exported at the top level.
